Raw Client Material:

Discovery call notes, 6 October 2026 (fictional). Attendees: Dana Whitfield,
General Counsel, Tamarack Instruments (fictional); Ravi Okafor, CISO; Ingrid
Solberg, Head of Quality.

- Tamarack designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. HQ in
  the Netherlands; plants in the Netherlands and Germany; sales office in the
  United States. About 1,100 staff; Dana said revenue is "in the US$200 to
  300 million range".
- AI today: a customer service chatbot on the support portal is live
  (deployed). An AI visual inspection system on the German production line is
  in pilot. They plan to use AI for sales forecasting next year.
- Dana: "We are piloting, not scaling. I want governance in place before
  visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027."
- Ravi: they run an ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS; Ingrid runs the quality management
  system under ISO 9001. They would like to start ISO/IEC 42001 work next
  year.
- Dana named the EU AI Act and the GDPR as the rules they are watching.
- Internal audit reported in June 2026 that there is no inventory of AI
  systems.
- Constraints: budget approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year; customer
  data must stay in the EU; the German works council must be consulted before
  anything touches production staff.
- Who would attend: Dana, Ravi, Ingrid, the Head of Data (Tomas Reyes), the
  German plant manager and two internal auditors.
- Dana is the budget holder for this. Decision expected by 15 December 2026.

judgment_calls: I treated 'internal audit function' as an asserted incumbent function that the material does not state. The material only says internal audit produced a report, and the response itself calls the entry an inference, which conflicts with Rule 1 ('Never infer facts'). Another scorer could read the June 2026 audit report as enough to show an internal audit program exists, and could pass this entry.
I treated 'run by Ingrid Solberg' for the ISO 9001 QMS as traceable, because the notes say 'Ingrid runs the quality management system under ISO 9001'.
I treated 'go-live targeted for Q2 2027' under STATED_CONSTRAINTS as an acceptable restatement of Dana's quote, not as a new fact.
I did not treat the AI_MATURITY value 'Piloting' as a fail. It matches Dana's own statement, and the response flags the tension with the deployed chatbot in CONFIDENCE_NOTES.
score.reasoning: The format, field completeness and halt logic are all correct. The case still fails because of one entry. INCUMBENT_FRAMEWORKS adds 'internal audit function', which the source does not state, and the response says it inferred it. Scorer guidance v1.14.3 counts incumbent functions the Profile Block does not state as failures. The case fails on Checklist item 3 and on the fail indicator for a Client fact beyond the framework names. Partial compliance is a FAIL.
